title: The Man Who Died for Lying in Church — Acts 5:1–10
paragraphs: The Man Who Died for Lying in Church — Acts 5:1–10
He died for pretending to be holy.

Acts 5:1–10 gives us one of the most terrifying moments in the New Testament: Ananias walked into church with an offering in his hand… and a lie in his heart. He wanted the image of surrender without the cost of surrender. He wanted to look devoted without actually being devoted. And before the congregation, God exposed what nobody else could see.

Because this story is not mainly about money. It is about hypocrisy. It is about the dangerous desire to be praised as spiritual while secretly clinging to sin. Ananias and Sapphira were not judged because they kept part of the land. Peter made that clear. They were judged because they lied to God and tried to dress deception in the clothes of worship.
The same God who judged them is the same God who sent His Son for liars like us.
That is the scandal of grace.

We have all done it in some way. Raised our hands with cold hearts. Said “I’m fine” while hiding compromise. Tried to look clean in public while rotting in private. But Jesus did not come for polished performers. He came for sinners who will tell the truth, fall on their knees, and repent.
The warning of Acts 5 is severe.
But the invitation of the Gospel is stronger.
Do not fake your way through the presence of God. Come clean. Bring the real mess. Bring the secret sin. Bring the double life. Because the blood of Jesus can cleanse what your image never could.
God is not looking for your performance.
And when truth meets the cross, mercy speaks louder than shame.
